en: So how do you use Ollama to run OpenAI
models on your system?
Well, if you run the Ollama command in your
terminal, in your command line,
you'll see a bunch of available commands
that you can combine with the Ollama
command.
For example, the very important run command,
which can be used to run a model, as we
learn here.
And that's indeed the command we need to
execute well, to run a large language model
on our system here.
So ollama run,
but then what?
Well, then you need to specify the model
identifier of the model that you wanna run
here.
And you find that in the models catalog on
the Ollama website, so on ollama.com.
Now, there also are other ways of creating
models or of running models locally, but
I'll get back to those later. Using the
models catalog is the most straightforward
and standard way of running models with
Ollama.
So if you go here, you'll see a list of
supported AI models. And it's a very, very
long list because Ollama essentially
supports all the popular and important open
large language models you also find on
Hugging Face.
And indeed, the Ollama team typically is
pretty fast when it comes to adding support
for a new model. So therefore, in this
Ollama models catalog here, you typically
find all the important, latest, and most
popular open large language models you can
run with Ollama.
For example, here you also find DeepSeek R1,
including the big one.
And I'll get back to these different
versions here in a second, but you could in
theory run the large one, the one that shook
up the AI industry in early 2025, with
Ollama, though I will say that even with
quantization, you probably don't have the
hardware to run that.
But all these smaller models,
especially up to the 32 billion parameters,
would definitely be doable, depending on the
kind of hardware you have, of course.
And then there are plenty of other popular
models as well.
For example, Mistral models, LLaMA models,
the Gemma 3, and also the older Gemma
models, which are really amazing. Which do
have vision capabilities, so which can also
be used to analyze images, for example.
And you can in general, of course, simply
browse that catalog to find out which model
sounds most interesting to you.
As mentioned, you can also run models in
another way, and I'll get back to that
later, but this official model catalog is a
good start.
